newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tougher gas oil rules seen boosting Japan imports.
newsitem.headline: Tougher gas oil rules seen boosting Japan imports.

text.p: Tougher Japanese regulations on sulphur content in gas oil are expected to boost low-sulphur gas oil imports, especially in the spring and fall, traders said on Tuesday.
Japan plans to lower the maximum allowable sulphur content in gas oil to 0.05 percent from 0.2 percent this year.
Gas oil cargoes shipped out of domestic refineries have to meet the new standard by July 1, and at the retail level the stringent regulations go into effect on October 1.

Oil firms can import high-sulphur cargoes and adjust the sulphur content as long as their refineries are up and running, because they have already revamped their plants to comply with the new regulations.

However, during routine maintenance checks, which peak in the spring and fall in Japan, refiners are expected to seek low-sulphur gas oil that can be marketed in Japan without the need for adjustments, traders said.
South Korea and Algeria are likely to be major suppliers of low-sulphur gas oil as they are currently capable of producing gas oil with less than 0.05 percent sulphur content, they said.
Although the United States has the expertise to meet the new standard, import prices for U.S. cargoes are expected to be less competitive than Algerian and South Korean prices, they added.
